This module introduces no new regulation, standard, or framework, and no new source was fetched for
it. It is pure synthesis: one joint presentation, built from everything this course and two prior
courses already locked about the Brookfield incident and the device-management platform vendor. The
links below are the direct inputs this module draws on; read any of them for the actual mechanics,
citations, and reasoning this lesson references by name but doesn't redevelop.

- **[ITIL-to-QSE crosswalk: change and
  problem](../itil-to-qse-crosswalk-change-and-problem/index.qmd)** (this course's module 1) —
  where change enablement was mapped onto change control, and problem management onto CAPA,
  including the exact distinction (a known-error record can sit indefinitely; a CAPA can't) this
  module reuses when flagging the deployment-sequencing fix as not yet an open CAPA.

- **[ITIL-to-QSE crosswalk: CMDB and continual
  improvement](../itil-to-qse-crosswalk-cmdb-and-continual-improvement/index.qmd)** (this course's
  module 2) — where a CMDB's qualification/validation-status field was first built out for the
  eQMS (electronic quality-management system), the same discipline this module's CIO half gestures
  toward for the device fleet.

- **[ITIL-to-GRC crosswalk](../itil-to-grc-crosswalk/index.qmd)** (this course's module 3) — the
  source of the one clean ISO 27001 Annex A match (access control) and the two domains with no
  counterpart (supplier relationships, business continuity) this module's "three lenses, live"
  section reuses as the same honest boundary, now applied to the vendor relationship instead of the
  eQMS.

- **[Building an inspection-ready service catalog and
  CMDB](../building-an-inspection-ready-service-catalog-and-cmdb/index.qmd)** (this course's module
  4) — where the "satisfies two reviewers fully, one honestly partial" shape was first proven for
  the eQMS. This module's own three-lens check is the identical pattern, found again.

- **[Translating ITSM and risk metrics for
  executives](../translating-itsm-and-risk-metrics-for-executives/index.qmd)** (this course's
  module 5) — the dual-audience translation model (fixed facts: finding, owner, date, closure rule;
  variable: framing and emphasis) this module reuses structurally, extended from two separate
  meetings to one joint room.

- **[Investigating a healthcare data
  incident](../../healthcare-security-and-privacy/investigating-a-healthcare-data-incident/index.qmd)**
  (`healthcare-security-and-privacy`) — the Brookfield incident's own closed investigation: the
  final 164.402 breach determination, the permanently unresolved encryption status, and the ranked
  root cause (deployment-sequencing gap, physical-handling gap, minimum-necessary gap). Every fact
  in this module's shared spine traces back to this lesson, unaltered.

- **[Supplier qualification and risk
  tiering](../../vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/supplier-qualification-and-risk-tiering/index.qmd)**,
  **[reading a SOC 2
  report](../../vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/reading-a-soc-2-report/index.qmd)**,
  **[reading an ISO 27001
  certificate](../../vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/reading-an-iso-27001-certificate/index.qmd)**,
  **[business associate
  agreements](../../vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/business-associate-agreements/index.qmd)**,
  and **[vendor change notifications and your own change
  control](../../vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/vendor-change-notifications-and-your-own-change-control/index.qmd)**
  (`vendor-and-third-party-risk-management`) — the device-management platform vendor's full file:
  its High tier, its SOC 2 and ISO 27001 findings, its plausible BAA requirement and the full
  (e)(2)(ii)(A)–(J) checklist, and the still-undecided change-notification clause. This module
  states every one of these findings exactly as that course left them.

- **[Coaching your QA and reporting
  upward](../../directing-the-quality-analyst/coaching-and-reporting-upward/index.qmd)**
  (`directing-the-quality-analyst`) — the review discipline this module's closing "what this means
  for your job" section points back to when it asks you to review your QA's and systems
  administrator's prep work for defensibility, not just polish.
